# Set up the project

## 1. Get the complete project

For this review, download the attached `single-cell-scaffold-review.zip` and extract it. Open the extracted `ai-assisted-single-cell-analysis` folder in VS Code (**File → Open Folder**) or RStudio. Do not work inside the ZIP.

Once this project has been published on GitHub, use the repository's **Code → Download ZIP** button. The final repository URL must be added here before release; no repository is assumed to exist yet.

You should see `_quarto.yml`, `data/`, `scripts/` and `examples/` directly inside the selected folder. Open **Terminal → New Terminal** in VS Code. Run every terminal command in this guide from this main project folder.

## 2. Install the tools

Install [R](https://cran.r-project.org/) and [Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/). RStudio is optional. Confirm these terminal commands work:

```bash
Rscript --version
quarto --version
```

## 3. Create the project environment

```bash
Rscript scripts/R/setup.R
```

The first setup installs packages and creates a genuine `renv.lock` for your R/Bioconductor combination. An internet connection is required. A tested release will include that lockfile. This review scaffold deliberately has no invented lockfile.

When a lockfile is supplied, the same command restores it. Commit `renv.lock`, `.Rprofile`, `renv/activate.R`, `renv/settings.json` and `renv/.gitignore` after validation. Keep the local package library out of Git. Do not refresh the lockfile merely to silence an installation error.

## 4. Start with synthetic data

```bash
Rscript scripts/R/prepare_synthetic.R
Rscript scripts/R/check_inputs.R synthetic
Rscript scripts/R/run_workflow.R synthetic
Rscript scripts/R/verify_cell.R synthetic Cell001
quarto preview
```

The book explains commands without executing them during rendering. Running analysis scripts creates your figures first. If a figure does not appear, run the relevant workflow; rendering the book does not generate data.
